findings.finding: Acceptance B4 requires "a project created from it builds, tests with pytest and Playwright on the served pane and needs no deploy." No automated test scaffolds a project from the profile and runs it; the completeness record itself marks this "untestable" and defers the live proof to campaign unit B7. The scaffolding guidance in `step-7-scaffolding.md` is prompt prose only (it even instructs the agent to hand-write `playwright.config.ts` because the shared template's default port is wrong — a known trap with no code or test preventing a scaffolded project from inheriting port 3000).
findings.suggestion: Either land a minimal generated-project acceptance test (scaffold in tmp_path, assert `/api/health` responds and the runner commands execute) or record the AC as explicitly deferred in the campaign status rather than satisfied.

findings.finding: The F17 blockers "smoke default" and "Browser Verify without a dev server" are cleared purely by documentation — the precedence chain "dev_url → env → profile dev_server → :3000" and the `--url http://localhost:3900` instruction exist only in prose read by an agent; no code path enforces them. The external plan review flagged exactly this (medium, "docs-only fix assumes the runner already reads the profile's port") and the disposition says "confirmed prompt-resolved," which is weaker than the spec's framing ("URL/health path now taken from the profile's dev_server before the :3000 default"). If an agent skips the prose, the failure mode is silent probing of port 3000.
findings.suggestion: At minimum add a unit test that `smoke_test.py --url`/browser-verify argument derivation exists as claimed, or move the profile-port resolution into a shared helper the prose invokes, so the invariant is pinned in code, not in prompt text.

findings.finding: The `testing` block carries a stray top-level `"command": "uv run pytest"` alongside the per-layer `unit.command` and `e2e.command`. It is consumed by nothing in the diff and any future loader that reads `testing.command` as a default (as other profiles may use it) would silently run pytest for undeclared layers instead of skipping them with a reason — contradicting the skip behavior the new runner test pins.
findings.suggestion: Remove the stray key, or verify what existing profiles/consumers do with `testing.command` and match it.

findings.finding: Unlike the `_SHARED` entry, which the module deliberately removes after importing ("shared/scripts holds a `tools` package that would shadow this plugin's own"), the appended `_LIB` (the plugin's own `scripts/lib`) is left on `sys.path` permanently. If two plugins follow this pattern, same-named sibling modules (e.g. `profile_consumer`, `command_runner`) from different plugins collide first-wins, and any module named like a stdlib/shared module in `scripts/lib` shadows it for everything imported afterwards.
findings.suggestion: Import via a package-qualified path or pop `_LIB` after the import, mirroring the existing `_SHARED` hygiene.

findings.finding: The test asserts `out["skipped"] is True` and the profile name appears in `skip_reason`, but never asserts the pgtap layer did not execute `npx`/npm or that `command` is absent/None. A regression where undeclared layers silently fall back to the npm default (the exact F17-class failure this change is about) would still pass unless skip_reason text changed.
findings.suggestion: Also assert the record contains no command/exit_code implying a run occurred (e.g. `out.get("command") in (None, "")` and `out["passed"] == 0` with the skip reason present), so a silent default-command run fails loudly.  Overall: the approach (data-only profile, no loader branches, deliberate empty backend, pinned no-default-leak test) is sound and the extraction looks genuinely behavior-preserving, but the acceptance criterion's end-to-end proof is deferred to another unit and two of the five F17 blockers are cleared by prose only — ship-with-fixes.  SHIPWRIGHT_VERDICT: revise
